messages:
ashok: Heads-up — noticed a weird regression in the quantized-ggml run on the new promptset. Quality dropped and CI shows a ton of examples with identical completions. suspect leakage between train/test splits. logs: `eval-runner-shard-3` shows duplicate IDs across shards.
maria: can you paste a minimal repro & which commit? failing job is `ci/eval/runner-shard-3` in the matrix.
ben: pasting snippet from the runner logs: `Shard 3: loaded 2048 items, overlaps detected: 43` then later `seed=42` and another process says `seed=4242`. looks like RNG not pinned across processes.
sofia: ugh — that would explain nondeterministic sharding. quick notes: our dataset manifest currently just lists paths and split tags; no file-level fingerprinting. if sharding is nondet you can easily get cross-split duplicates. propose: 1) add file-level sha256 in manifest, 2) add split fingerprints (hash of ids per split), 3) a lightweight leakage check in the harness.
eval-bot: ci/eval/runner-shard-3 failed 1 job — see https://ci.redwood/s/4821 — flaky failure count: 2/10 in last 24h.
ashok (correction): @maria meant @ashok — sorry typo.
ashok: (note: mistaken name, continue)
ashok: here's a short SQL I ran locally to find duplicates across splits: ```sql
select id, array_agg(distinct split) as splits, count(*) as cnt
from dataset.index
group by id
having count(distinct split) > 1;
```
maria: good catch. if we add a CI guard that runs the above query (or equivalent mapreduce) and fails on duplicates > 0 we can catch regressions early. threshold maybe 0 for train/test, allow tiny duplicates inside same split.
ben: root cause for shard nondeterminism: eval-runner used `random.shuffle` in multiple processes without seeding with a per-job seed. fix: use numpy's RNG with a job-scoped seed + assign deterministic start offsets per shard. small patch: ```python
# before
random.shuffle(items)
# after
rng = np.random.default_rng(job_seed)
items = rng.permutation(items)
```
ryan: for dashboards/alerts — let's add `duplicate_prompt_rate` to the eval metrics. emit at job-level: duplicates / total and fire an alert if > 0.1% for train/test or > 1% for validation. that will be easier for SOC to triage.
ci-bot: Opening ticket: EVAL-1248 dataset-leakage-check added to eval pipeline (auto-created).
maria: I'll open a PR for the runner patch + CI guard. PR #4832 — brief diff in the SHA manifest check: ```diff
+  - path: data/prompts-v2.jsonl
+    sha256: 9f2b...
+    split: test
```
ben: also add a small unit test to the eval-harness CI that generates a synthetic fixture with guaranteed overlap and asserts the guard fails. helps avoid regressions from refactors. example: `tests/test_leakage_guard.py` with a tempfile manifest.
sofia: I'll regenerate the canonical fixtures (we should bump to prompts-v2.1) and upload to the test bucket. note: when regenerating, run `scripts/regen_fixtures --seed 2026` and publish checksums.
ashok (again, typo): disregard name confusion earlier.
ashok: next steps summary: @maria opens PR #4832 for runner RNG + CI guard, @sofia publishes v2.1 fixtures+manifest, @ben adds unit test, @ryan wires duplicate_prompt_rate to dashboard + alert. We'll block the quantized model bring-up until CI is green and duplicate rate is 0 for train/test.
maria: ack — will aim to have PR + branch CI by EOD. tagging @sofia for manifest upload.
sofia: will do, I'll also add a short release note in `platform/CHANGELOG.md` about the dataset fingerprinting and leakage guard.
ryan: small ops ask — can we add the new metric to the SLO dashboard but keep alerts in `info` for 48h while we roll out? then escalate to `warning` if stable.
ashok: good plan. thanks everyone. can we schedule a 20-min sync tomorrow 10:30 to quick-check CI post-merge?
maria: yes. invite sent. :calendar:
